In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dihadron spectrum is a very sensitive probe to the jet energy loss in the medium.
dihadron production at RHIC is more sensitive to the energy loss of the jet than the single hadronic production, whereas the opposite is the case at the LHC.

the dihadron spectra at LHC are expected to be more sensitive to the energy loss parameter and the initial parton distributions than the single hadrons, and the latter to be more sensitive than the dihadrons at RHIC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dihadron suppression at RHIC/LCH can be understood as a result of both the energy loss of the jet shower partons and the punch-through jets.
